title: Merge overlapping contact cards
prompt:
Merge contact cards (lists of identifier strings) that share any identifier, directly or through a chain of cards, and return each resulting person's sorted identifiers.

- 0 to 10,000 cards, each with 1 to 10 lowercase ASCII identifiers such as emails or handles; a card may repeat an identifier.
- Write each person as the ascending list of their distinct identifiers.
- Sort people by their first (smallest) identifier. Strings compare by character code, so "b@x" < "bob@x".
hints: Think of identifiers as nodes. A card says all of its identifiers belong together.
Use union-find keyed by identifier: union every identifier on a card with that card's first identifier.
After all unions, group identifiers by their root, sort each group, then sort the groups by their first element.

solution.explanation: Union-find over identifiers merges every card into one set per person, including chains where cards only overlap indirectly. A card's root stays the root while that card is processed, so all its identifiers end up in one set. No identifier belongs to two people, so sorting people by their first identifier gives a unique order.

complexity.notes: N is the total number of identifiers. The unions take O(N log N) worst case with path halving alone (near-linear with union by size too); the final sorting is O(N log N) either way.

followUps: Each card also carries a display name, and two people with the same name must stay separate unless they share an identifier. What changes?
How would you solve this with a graph search instead of union-find?
